opener.h1: Plan the journey to your Conditional Access baseline.
opener.intro: IAMAI reads a Microsoft Entra tenant, compares it with a published Conditional Access baseline, and writes a dated plan to close the gaps without locking anyone out. It is read-only and runs in this browser.
opener.builtFor: The person doing security at a small MSP or a small business, on their own, who has to get this done in a few weeks.
catches: An admin whose only sign-in method is a text message, about to be required to use a passkey.
An emergency access account inside the policy it exists to survive.
A country rule that blocks the person who wrote it.
A service account that a legacy-authentication block stops at 2 a.m.
A meeting-room device that a session rule signs out every hour.

removing: Entra admin center → Entra ID → Enterprise applications.
opener.tip: Sign in with a Global Administrator or Global Reader account. Entra ID P1 adds sign-in evidence; the plan works without it.
cantCatch: Devices that send mail without signing in: Direct Send printers, scanners and some applications. Nothing appears in the records, so a legacy-authentication block can stop one the plan never listed. Ask whoever manages printing and scan-to-email; the step asks before that block enforces.

Authentication that happens outside Entra: a federated domain, third-party MFA, applications against on-premises AD. Entra records the sign-in but not what the other system enforced. Check the domain list for federation and the other system's own console.

Anything on a longer cycle than the collected records: the quarterly invoice run, the yearly renewal job. It exists, it authenticates, and it has left no evidence yet. Where those exist, keep new blocks in report-only across a full business cycle.
Credentials saved on equipment nobody has touched in years: routers, NAS boxes, UPS cards, an old copier. They surface the day something blocks them; a walk through the comms room beats any report.
What a partner's own tenant enforces for their people. IAMAI sees their sign-ins here, never their controls; the guest steps ask how much to trust them.

steps.why: Emergency access accounts are how you keep access to {tenant} if a change goes wrong.

decision.help: Tick every account that exists only for this purpose; two are needed. IAMAI nominated these from their names, roles and exclusions. Create the rest below.

whatToDo.lead: Fix each failing check, top to bottom. {failing} of {total} checks fail today.
create: Entra admin center → Entra ID → Users → New user. Name it so the purpose is obvious ({exampleName}).
Sign-in address on the tenant's own onmicrosoft.com domain; cloud-only; no licence; no department, title or manager.
Roles → assign Global Administrator, active and permanent.

Set a passphrase of at least 20 random characters. Store it offline in two places that different people can reach without signing in to this tenant, for example a sealed envelope in a safe and a second copy with the business owner. Never in a mailbox, a chat, or a password manager that needs this tenant to sign in.
Register a hardware security key (FIDO2) for each account and keep it with the passphrase. Not a passkey in Authenticator: that lives on a person's phone. Do not share a key between accounts.

checkFixes.second-account: Create a second account: one account is a single point of failure.
checkFixes.permanent-global-admin: {name}: assign Global Administrator permanently and actively; an eligible role has to activate first, and activation is one of the things a bad policy can block.
checkFixes.cloud-only: {name}: this account is synced from on-premises; recreate it as cloud-only.
checkFixes.onmicrosoft-domain: {name}: move the sign-in address to {onmicrosoftDomain}; a custom domain depends on DNS and on any federation.
checkFixes.excluded-everywhere: {name} is inside {list:policies}: add the exclusions group to each policy's Users → Exclude → Groups in Create or Correct Exclusions Group. Do not exclude the account itself.
checkFixes.no-dynamic-group: {name} is a member of the dynamic group {group}, which a policy targets; remove it or change the rule.
checkFixes.mfa-method: {name}: register a hardware security key (see step 5 above).
checkFixes.shared-authenticator: {name} shares the Authenticator device {device} with {otherAccount}; move it to its own security key or passkey.
checkFixes.not-a-person: {name} looks like a person's account (it has {attribute}); use a dedicated account instead.
checkFixes.report-only-excluded: The report-only policies {list:policies} do not exclude the exclusions group either; same fix, in Create or Correct Exclusions Group.
checkFixes.managed-policies-excluded: The Microsoft-managed policies {list:policies} do not exclude the exclusions group; Microsoft turns these on itself. Same fix, in Create or Correct Exclusions Group.
checkFixes.phishing-resistant: {name}: register a hardware security key; text and call codes are taken by a swapped SIM.
checkFixes.method-diversity: Both accounts depend on {method} alone; give one of them a different method type.
checkFixes.auth-methods-migration: Finish migrating to the authentication methods policy (the per-user MFA setting can block a recovery sign-in): Entra admin center → Entra ID → Authentication methods → Policies → Manage migration → Migration complete.
checkFixes.no-licence-no-mailbox: {name} holds {licence}; remove it. An emergency account needs no mailbox.
checkFixes.recent-sign-in: {name} last signed in {ago}; run the drill (Cleanup) once the checks pass.
checkFixes.display-name: {name}: rename so the purpose is obvious to whoever finds it next, for example {exampleName}.

lockedOut.label: If a change locks you out
steps: Sign in with one of the emergency accounts above, in a private browser window.
Entra admin center → Entra ID → Conditional Access → Policies → open the policy that changed today → Enable policy: Report-only (or Off) → Save. It applies within minutes.

If the portal itself is blocked: sign in from a device and network the policies trust (a managed laptop on the office network), or from any device run Connect-MgGraph -Scopes Policy.ReadWrite.ConditionalAccess and then Update-MgIdentityConditionalAccessPolicy -ConditionalAccessPolicyId <id> -State enabledForReportingButNotEnforced.
If no route works, Microsoft support can help; they will ask for the tenant id: {tenantId}.
